question.problem: Given the inequalities $3<x<7$ and $2\le x\le 5$, express their common set of solutions as an interval.
question.worked_solution:
We start by sketching the solutions to the two inequalities separately:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/468dea33da7365430c2e08bcbf13d176fdafabf64aaac0a940a01c108b1b0e64.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/413c2bbe7a61c8983ea92ff4bb73bba27fc05856eae5f1fdb9614aa2b50f92aa.png)

The common set of values consists of the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/51a4f2d24dd17ae11e1530b6765782163b9c8f79b69509b458037e747ae0dd37.png)

Therefore, the common set of values is
$(3,5].$
